item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 23 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae starts a fourth Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance run and happily dives into Tokyo Tower progress, side quests, and lore-heavy story speculation.

Sey counters Grand Theft Auto VI fever with five crime-flavored indies, from Retro City Rampage and Shakedown: Hawaii to Promise Mascot Agency.

Bhagpuss side-eyes the Grand Theft Auto VI takeover of blogland, while admitting Lana Del Rey hosting an in-game radio station is weirdly tempting.

Marc revisits MadWorld to ask why ultra-violent Wii games felt like smart bets, even when niche realities kept that market smaller than hoped.

Wilhelm rounds up Fantasy Critic chaos as Grand Theft Auto VI drops a monster 98.7 and steamrolls a week otherwise crowded with small PC indies.

The Chronicler digs into Coast Watchers after three plays, highlighting its hidden-information spy-vs-patrol design and strong South Pacific intelligence theme.

Tobold finds low-level Pathfinder: Kingmaker spellcasters weirdly incentivized to use crossbows, especially once digital combat pacing burns through spell slots.

Warner’s weekly reading stack is a pretty grim but sharp tour through AI anxiety, tech failures, and politics getting uglier together.

Juhis has a low-output Djangonaut week, but still finds perspective, team camaraderie, and a nice community win around Django and Raffaella Suardini.

Bruce Schneier argues AI companies keep dodging accountability by treating chatbot output as protected speech when convenient and mere machine error otherwise.

Dave Winer shares fresh BonBon progress, WordPress integration plans, and a bigger pitch for a simpler Markdown-based web for writers.

Kimimi gets candid about Twine nerves, reminding herself that interactive fiction is still real design even when it looks like just words and choices.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 22 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae finishes mopping up Divinity: Original Sin 2’s Wrecker’s Cove with more Deathfog, dead dwarves, and the usual inventory-management comedown.

Cliffski launches Ridiculous Space Battles into Early Access, reflects on hobby-dev freedom, and vents about the ugly toxicity that still dogs game releases.

Bhagpuss returns to Wuthering Waves on GeForce Now, then gets sidetracked by its surprisingly full-on school-life sim, Second Coming of Solaris: Unwritten Dreams.

Wilhelm rounds up EVE Online’s quiet season with Deteriorated’s Alliance Tournament win and an October MER showing Crimson Harvest’s smaller-than-usual economic bump.

Tobold unboxes an absurdly lavish storage vault for The Elder Scrolls: Betrayal of the Second Era and cheerfully admits it’s pure whale behavior.

Ramen Junkie’s weekly wrap-up hops from Rings of Power and SWAT Exiles to Blokees, a Transformers Advent calendar, and a Batman Hush Catwoman kit.

WCRobinson shares a two-week India trip that nearly died at Heathrow over a visa error before turning into a photo-heavy family holiday.

Roger shares a Windows shortcut trick to open Discord straight to your chosen server and channel, skipping the app’s Quests page.

Bruce Schneier’s post veers into a comment-thread dive on logic, Gödel, Turing machines, and why computers can’t fully verify their own foundations.

Dave Winer spotlights new Markdown-powered sites and BonBon demos, with a little evangelism for lightweight publishing on the side.

Cristian admits he’s drifting back to Google Translate and other Big Tech services because they’re simply faster and easier than the alternatives.

Patrick pokes at what’s “hot” in indie RPGs, contrasting giant names like Daggerheart and Dungeon Crawler Carl with the small-press scene.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 21 November 2026
item.description:
Tipa says Final Fantasy Resonance distills Brave Exvius into a cleaner, turn-based adventure that keeps the crystals, chocobos, and Visions while ditching the gacha sprawl.

Sey rounds up Dice Have No Eyes and Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed, then gushes over GTA 6 as a delayed blockbuster that looks worth the wait.

Heartless is impressed by Grand Theft Auto VI’s Leonida and story, but hopes the launch-day quick-time feel gives way to proper sandbox chaos.

Kimimi spotlights Kaisoku Tenshi: Super Sonic, a weird PS1 platformer-beat ’em up where speed, inertia, and dash-kicks matter more than obscurity suggests.

Zack finds Assassin’s Creed Rogue Remastered’s Templar-switch premise promising, but says the French and Indian War spin-off earns its long-standing bad reputation.

Wilhelm is happily lost in WoW Forever’s familiar routines, wondering whether Blizzard’s hook is novelty or just the timeless alt-making treadmill.

Jimmy revisits how Diablo II expanded Blizzard North’s hellish loot loop without losing the brutal simplicity that made the first game so hard to quit.

Kelly trades games for real-life teardown mode, documenting a big landscaping reset of flower beds, trees, and long-neglected backyard boxes.

Frank uses SET, the Riemann Hypothesis, and AI to riff on how solving problems may be messier and more human than neat theory allows.

UltrViolet recaps Week 10 with Commanders playoff math, strong alternate teams, and an AI fantasy win powered by Jayden Daniels, James Cook, and Cam Skattebo.

Tim Bray sketches AI’s current sweet spot as 'singleton apps'—useful one-person software projects—while doubting that niche scales to most real-world development.

David turns caddisworm larvae into fantasy fuel, imagining silk-glued armor, battlefield scraps, and treasure-hoarding 'caddiswyrms' straight out of a monster manual.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 19 November 2026
item.description:
Stargrace dives into Wurm Online’s Jackal with three characters, chasing weapon smithing, archaeology, caverns, and a welcome break from getting bullied by worgs.

Bhagpuss says Neverness To Everness’s Once Upon A Glitched Call is basically an anime movie, but an unexpectedly brilliant one.

Krista falls back into League of Legends through K/DA, Arcane season 2, and the surprisingly tempting Riftbound TCG.

Shintar’s WoW Forever paladin tackles Verigan’s Fist with guilds, pugs, and repeated sub-quest faceplants that turn routine runs into comedy.

Scopique says Star Citizen salvaging with the Galaxy and Salvation is chill and profitable, while the Liberator still feels awkward and not especially useful.

Wilhelm and Potshot take Over the Hill to Algeria, where sand, rocks, and unmarked routes make exploration feel a lot less straightforward than snowy Canada.

The Chronicler teaches Mike Lambo’s Commander: Romans v Dacians through a full scenario, praising its Roman theme, random setups, and deadly commander risk.

Tobold uses GTA VI’s huge acclaim to ask whether great games come from genius, or just enough time, money, and competent project management.

CrazyKinux is all-in on Nuremberg, an AI-made sci-fi trailer mashing the 1561 sky mystery with alternate WWII, time travel, and Tesla.

Jeff explains why he joined the NTP Pool with a Stratum 2 server, plus the uptime, exposure, and long-tail traffic headaches volunteers should expect.

Warner weighs the ‘patchpocalypse’ theory that AI-driven bug hunting is surfacing vulnerability floods faster than patching can safely keep up.

Dave Winer says BonBon’s first day went great, with a demo already showing how Markdown sites and old archives can look in its writer-friendly web.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 18 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae chips away at Divinity: Original Sin 2’s Wrecker’s Cove, unimpressed by Void grossness but delighted by teleporting a shark onto land.

Roger argues ballooning installs like GTA 6’s 212GB sting more now that SSD prices have shot up and upgrades feel out of reach.

Frostilyte likes Two & Two Agents as a playful asymmetric co-op puzzler, especially its communication-driven demo and clever encoded-language puzzles.

Joel warmly recommends playing Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye completely blind, calling it a beautifully integrated extra adventure worth savoring later.

Marc highlights how Wario Land: Shake It! turned the Wii’s non-HD limits into a strength with lavish hand-drawn 2D animation.

Tobold revisits Pathfinder: Kingmaker as comfort gaming, praising kineticist while grumbling that its story companions are awkward enough to tempt some light modding.

Ramen Junkie dives into the Jem x Transformers Blaster set, especially the gloriously weird Kiss Players cassette references and its unexpectedly sharp deco.

Cristian posts a quick meme shot titled 3 Body Problem, more gallery wink than essay.

Bhagpuss admits cheaping out on a Baldur's Gate 3-capable PC backfired, then says ChatGPT surprisingly helped rescue the machine.

Warner says Face Unlock on the iPhone Duo boosts convenience, but it also muddies Apple’s usual security-first line versus proper Face ID.

Bruce Schneier points to reporting that France’s refrigerator cyberattacks are being tied to Iran, though the U.S. assessment is still only low-confidence.

Dave Winer tees up BonBon’s release and pitches it, with help from Claude Code, as a writer-first web project aimed squarely at tech’s usual mess.
